Imitation

/im-ih-TAY-shuhn/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Imitation means a copy or fake version of something, made to look like the real or original thing

The bracelet's stones turned out to be high-quality glass imitations, not the real emeralds the seller had claimed.

Worked Example

When the museum's insurers demanded tighter security, curators quietly swapped the original 400-year-old necklace for a museum-grade imitation crafted from cubic zirconia, storing the genuine piece in an undisclosed vault while visitors admired the convincing fake on display.

The piece on display looks identical to the original but isn't — it's a deliberately crafted substitute, which is exactly what "imitation" names.

How Imitation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

replica

replica: often implies a careful, detailed reproduction, especially of art or historical objects

knockoff

knockoff: a casual, often disapproving word for a cheap unauthorized copy

fake

fake: the plainest, most direct word for something not genuine

Antonyms

original

original: the first, genuine version something is copied from

authentic

authentic: genuinely real, not a copy or substitute

How Strong Is It? — knockoff → replica → imitation

knockoff vs. imitation

knockoff vs. imitation: A knockoff is usually a cheap, unauthorized copy, made quickly and sold at a lower price.

replica vs. imitation

replica vs. imitation: A replica is often a carefully made, high-quality reproduction, sometimes even authorized by the original creator.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — imit-

Root — imit-: to copy (same root as imitate, taught earlier in this unit)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or result of

Put it together

Put it together: Just as "imitate" means "to copy," "imitation" names the result of that act — the copy itself, produced by the same imit- root taught earlier in this unit.

Use the root in a new word: imitator

Use the root in a new word: imitator: The talent show's most popular act was an imitator who could reproduce six different singers' voices in under two minutes.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral to slightly negative

Imitation is often neutral (an 'imitation leather' couch is simply described honestly), but it can also carry a mildly negative edge when used to point out that something isn't genuine, as in 'a cheap imitation of the real thing.'
